accepted.s: The name of the Tuluva dynasty is derived from:
accepted.x: The Tuluva dynasty was named after Tulunadu, identified in the material with the Mysore region.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the geographical source of a dynastic name.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s: Tulunadu was conquered by Harihara in which year?
accepted.x: Harihara conquered Tulunadu in 1342.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely spaced chronological figures.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tuluva dynasty:
1. Timmaraju was regarded as its progenitor.
2. Kannada was the mother tongue of its ruling family.
3. Telugu was not favoured in its court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Timmaraju was the progenitor, and Kannada was the mother tongue. Telugu was favoured, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses a language-related fact.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s: Who was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha?
accepted.x: Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, a Saluva general, was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler with the political role actually held.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s: Tuluva Narasa Nayaka died in:
accepted.x: Tuluva Narasa Nayaka died in 1503.
accepted.tq: Use a date-based elimination among neighbouring reign events.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s: Which event is referred to as the “second usurpation” in the history of the Tuluva dynasty?
o: Saluva Narasimha's seizure of the throne in 1485
Vira Narasimha's killing of Immadi Narasimha at Penugonda in 1505
accepted.x: The killing of Immadi Narasimha by Vira Narasimha at Penugonda in 1505 is identified as the second usurpation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similarly described usurpations.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s: Vira Narasimha is generally identified as the founder of the Tuluva dynasty because he:
o: founded the Sangama line after conquering Tulunadu
killed Immadi Narasimha and established Tuluva rule in 1505
served as the general of Saluva Narasimha in 1485
accepted.x: Vira Narasimha established Tuluva rule after killing Immadi Narasimha at Penugonda in 1505. Some accounts also describe Narasa Nayaka as the dynasty's progenitor or founder.
accepted.tq: Use the founding act rather than an associated predecessor to identify a dynasty founder.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rulers of the Tuluva dynasty in chronological order of succession:
A. Achyutaraya
B. Vira Narasimha
C. Sadasiva
D. Krishnadevaraya
accepted.x: The order was Vira Narasimha, Krishnadevaraya, Achyutaraya and Sadasiva.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last rulers, then arrange the intervening succession.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the succession and reign period of Krishnadevaraya?
accepted.x: Krishnadevaraya ruled from 1509 to 1529 and succeeded Vira Narasimha.
accepted.tq: Check the ruler against both the reign period and immediate predecessor.
accepted.sec: Tuluva dynasty - founder, succession, dynasty identification

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Timmakka, the wife of Annamacharya, wrote Subhadra Kalyanam in Telugu.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure poet–work pair and reject swapped literary associations.
accepted.sec: Royal women poets → work (Tirumalamba-Varadambika Parinayam, Gangadevi)

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Tirumalamba — Varadambika Parinayam
2. Ramabhadramba — Raghunathabhyudayam
3. Gangadevi — Madhura Vijayam
4. Timmakka — Subhadra Kalyanam
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Tirumalamba, Ramabhadramba, Gangadevi and Timmakka are associated respectively with the four listed works.
accepted.tq: Verify a complete literary matching set rather than relying on one familiar pair.
accepted.sec: Royal women poets → work (Tirumalamba-Varadambika Parinayam, Gangadevi)

accepted.s: Varadambika Parinayam deals with the marriage of:
accepted.x: Tirumalamba's Sanskrit work describes the marriage of Achyutaraya to Varadambika.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the subject of a work from its author and language.
accepted.sec: Royal women poets → work (Tirumalamba-Varadambika Parinayam, Gangadevi)

accepted.s: The term ‘Ashtadiggajas’ literally refers to the:
o: eight elephants supporting the eight directions
accepted.x: Ashtadiggajas means the eight elephants believed to support the eight directions; in Krishnadevaraya's court it referred to eight eminent poets.
accepted.tq: Separate the literal meaning of a term from its institutional application.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: The Ashtadiggajas were associated with which institution in Krishnadevaraya's court?
o: The eight pillar-poets of the Bhuvana Vijayam hall
The council of military governors at Penugonda
The body of provincial revenue officers
The group of eight Bahmani ambassadors
accepted.x: The Ashtadiggajas were the eight pillar-poets of Krishnadevaraya's court in the Bhuvana Vijayam hall.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional meaning of a famous collective title.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: The Tippalur inscription refers to the Ashtadiggajas as a:
accepted.x: The Tippalur inscription calls the Ashtadiggajas a Kavula Samstha, or institution of poets.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact technical expression associated with an inscription.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Panduranga Mahatmyam was written by Tenali Ramakrishna. Pingali Surana wrote Raghava Pandaviyamu and Kalapurnodayamu.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped author–work pair among closely related court poets.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Nandi Timmana is also known as:
accepted.x: Nandi Timmana is known as Mukku Timmana. Prabandha Parameshwara is identified with Errana, not Timmana.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a poet's popular name from a title belonging to another poet.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Pingali Surana — Raghava Pandaviyamu and Kalapurnodayamu
accepted.x: Pingali Surana wrote Raghava Pandaviyamu and Kalapurnodayamu. The other works belong to Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, Ramarajabhushana and Allasani Peddana respectively.
accepted.tq: Use author–work discrimination where several poets belong to the same literary court.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Raghava Pandaviyamu is noted for its:
o: account of the marriage of Varadambika
description of Shaiva worship at Kalahasti
accepted.x: Pingali Surana's Raghava Pandaviyamu is a dvyarthi kavya, employing a double meaning.
accepted.tq: Identify a distinctive literary feature rather than merely recalling an author.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ramarajabhushana, also called Bhattumurti, wrote Vasucharitramu and Narasabhupaliyamu.
accepted.tq: Start with a distinctive two-work association to solve the matching question.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Vasucharitra was dedicated to:
accepted.x: Vasucharitra, associated with Ramarajabhushana, was dedicated to Tirumala Raya.
accepted.tq: Match a literary dedication with its named patron.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Nandi Timmana?
o: He was titled Andhra Kavita Pitamaha and wrote Manucharitramu.
He was known as Mukku Timmana and wrote Parijatapaharanamu.
He wrote Raghava Pandaviyamu and was known for dvyarthi kavya.
He wrote Panduranga Mahatmyam and was the court wit.
accepted.x: Nandi Timmana, known as Mukku Timmana, wrote Parijatapaharanamu and was regarded as the king's favourite.
accepted.tq: Combine a poet's title or popular name with his work to avoid pair-swapping traps.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the literary identity of the poet?
accepted.x: Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu is associated with Ramabhyudayamu and Sakalakathasara Sangrahamu. Dvyarthi kavya is associated with Pingali Surana.
accepted.tq: Reject the borrowed literary description that belongs to a neighbouring poet.
accepted.sec: Ashtadiggajas - meaning, poet → work + title

accepted.s: Which title of Krishnadevaraya signifies his role in restoring the Bahmani Sultan?
accepted.x: Krishnadevaraya was called Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya for restoring the Bahmani Sultan.
accepted.tq: Match a title with the deed that caused it to be conferred.
accepted.sec: Titles of Krishnadevaraya; towns founded and their namesakes

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a title associated with Krishnadevaraya?
accepted.x: Andhra Kavita Pitamaha was the title conferred on Allasani Peddana. The other three are titles of Krishnadevaraya.
accepted.tq: Separate the ruler's titles from an honorific belonging to his court poet.
accepted.sec: Titles of Krishnadevaraya; towns founded and their namesakes

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Nagalapuram was named after Krishnadevaraya's mother Nagalamba.
accepted.tq: Match a foundation name with its namesake, avoiding queen–mother confusion.
accepted.sec: Titles of Krishnadevaraya; towns founded and their namesakes

accepted.s: Hospet was also known as Tirumaladevi-pattana because it was named after:
accepted.x: Hospet, or Tirumaladevi-pattana, was named after Queen Tirumaladevi.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named royal women and relatives.
accepted.sec: Titles of Krishnadevaraya; towns founded and their namesakes

accepted.s: The title ‘Radhamadhava Kavi’ was conferred on:
accepted.x: Chintalapudi Ellanarya received the title Radhamadhava Kavi.
accepted.tq: Match an uncommon literary title with its recipient.
accepted.sec: Titles of Krishnadevaraya; towns founded and their namesakes

accepted.s: What special honour did Krishnadevaraya himself bestow on Allasani Peddana?
o: He appointed him governor of Chandragiri.
He fixed the Gandapenderam anklet on Peddana's foot.
He made him commander of the Arab cavalry.
accepted.x: Krishnadevaraya personally fixed the Gandapenderam anklet on Allasani Peddana's foot.
accepted.tq: Recall a distinctive ceremonial act instead of a general patronage relationship.
accepted.sec: Titles of Krishnadevaraya; towns founded and their namesakes

accepted.s: Saluva Narasimha's usurpation of the Vijayanagara throne took place in:
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha seized the throne in 1485, an event described as the first usurpation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first usurpation date from the later Tuluva succession date.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Saluva Narasimha was the lord of which place when he launched his usurpation?
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha was the lord of Chandragiri when he sent Tuluva Narasa Nayaka to seize the throne.
accepted.tq: Identify the political base from which a ruler launched his action.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a major reason for Saluva Narasimha's usurpation?
o: The empire had abandoned its coastal territories voluntarily.
The Portuguese had occupied the Vijayanagara capital.
The empire was strengthened by a succession of powerful rulers after Devaraya II.
Weak rulers and invasions by the Gajapati and Bahmani powers weakened the kingdom.
accepted.x: After Devaraya II, weak rulers such as Virupaksha II and Praudha Raya were unable to resist Gajapati and Bahmani invasions, which weakened the kingdom.
accepted.tq: Link political weakness and external invasions to the resulting usurpation.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the rulers preceding Saluva Narasimha is correct?
o: Praudha Raya was the general who seized the throne for Saluva Narasimha.
Virupaksha II was described as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless.
Virupaksha II founded the Saluva dynasty, while Praudha Raya ruled from Chandragiri.
Both rulers successfully repelled the Gajapati and Bahmani invasions.
accepted.x: Nuniz described Virupaksha II as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless; their weakness contributed to the crisis of the kingdom.
accepted.tq: Match the correct description with each of two neighbouring rulers.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Saluva Narasimha was also known as:
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha was called Raya Maharasu.
accepted.tq: Recall the alternate title of a ruler rather than confusing it with a royal epithet of Krishnadevaraya.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Saluva Narasimha's rule?
o: 1505–1509, with the capital moved from Kalyanapuram to Udayagiri
1485–1491, with the capital moved from Kalyanapuram to Chandragiri
1491–1503, with the capital moved from Chandragiri to Penugonda
1485–1505, with the capital retained at Kalyanapuram
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha ruled from 1485 to 1491 and shifted the capital from Kalyanapuram to Chandragiri.
accepted.tq: Check a ruler against both reign dates and capital movement.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Which of the following territories were taken by Saluva Narasimha?
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha took Honnavar, Bhatkal and Mangalore during his rule.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct territorial cluster from a set of nearby medieval places.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Saluva Narasimha:
1. He brought Arab horses from Ormuz.
2. He introduced Samugaris, or gunmen.
3. He lost Udayagiri to Gajapati Purushottama.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Saluva Narasimha imported Arab horses from Ormuz, introduced gunmen called Samugaris, and lost Udayagiri to Gajapati Purushottama.
accepted.tq: Verify a cluster of military and territorial developments without reversing the outcome.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: The court poet of Saluva Narasimha was:
accepted.x: Rajanatha Dindima was the court poet of Saluva Narasimha and wrote Saluvabhyudayam.
accepted.tq: Match a ruler with the poet associated with his court.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Rajanatha Dindima wrote Saluvabhyudayam. The other pairings incorrectly exchange the works of royal women poets and Ashtadiggajas.
accepted.tq: Use a sure author–work pair to eliminate literary-name swaps.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Annamacharya was a contemporary of:
accepted.x: Annamacharya was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha.
accepted.tq: Connect a major saint-poet with the correct contemporary ruler.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - usurpation, reasons, Saluva rule, contemporary of Annamacharya

accepted.s: Annamacharya is associated with the composition of how many kirtanas dedicated to Venkateswara?
accepted.x: Annamacharya is associated with 32,000 kirtanas dedicated to Venkateswara.
accepted.tq: Recall a high-value quantitative fact with proportionate numerical distractors.
